name: South Africa
genZNote: South Africa has THREE capital cities (Pretoria, Cape Town, Bloemfontein) splitting executive, legislative, and judicial power across different regions — a genuinely unique compromise that echoes its complicated, negotiated path out of apartheid.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located at the southern tip of Africa, bordered by Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, and Eswatini, and entirely surrounding the independent kingdom of Lesotho.
Diverse terrain including the interior plateau (highveld), the dramatic Drakensberg mountain range, and coastlines on both the Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
Uniquely has three capital cities dividing government functions: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), and Bloemfontein (judicial).

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Has 12 official languages (as of 2023, after Sign Language was added), reflecting its extraordinary ethnic and cultural diversity, often called the 'Rainbow Nation'.
Diverse population includes Black African, White (Afrikaner and English-descended), Coloured (mixed-race), and Indian/Asian communities, each with distinct histories.
Nelson Mandela is a globally revered symbol of the country's transition from apartheid to democracy and reconciliation.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary republic with a President serving as both head of state and government, elected by the National Assembly rather than directly by voters.
Ended the apartheid system of institutionalised racial segregation in 1994 through the country's first fully democratic elections, won by Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC).
The Truth and Reconciliation Commission, chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu, became a globally studied model for addressing historical injustice through public testimony rather than only punishment.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Performed the world's first successful human-to-human heart transplant in 1967, led by South African surgeon Dr. Christiaan Barnard.
Africa's most industrially and scientifically advanced economy, with strong mining engineering, astronomy (hosting part of the Square Kilometre Array radio telescope), and biomedical research.
Led globally influential research and public health responses to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, given the scale of its domestic public health challenge.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A member of the G20 and the only African member of the BRICS grouping (alongside Brazil, Russia, India, China).
A regional leader in the African Union and Southern African Development Community (SADC).
Internationally recognised for its post-apartheid reconciliation model, though it continues to face significant domestic inequality challenges.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and South Africa share a 'Strategic Partnership' and are both BRICS members, with deep historical ties dating to Mahatma Gandhi's formative years of activism in South Africa (1893-1914).
Home to a significant ethnic Indian community, particularly in Durban, tracing back to 19th-century indentured labour migration.
Both countries collaborate closely on global governance reform, including advocacy for UN Security Council reform and Global South solidarity.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Africa's most industrialised economy, historically built on mining (gold, platinum, diamonds), alongside manufacturing, finance, and agriculture.
Home to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, Africa's largest, and a well-developed financial services sector.
Faces significant economic challenges including high unemployment and energy supply (electricity/load-shedding) constraints.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Nelson Mandela and the peaceful end of apartheid in 1994.
Being the only African member of BRICS and G20.
The world's first human heart transplant (1967).
Deep historical links to Mahatma Gandhi's early activism.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: South African Rand (ZAR).
The most industrialized economy in Africa, with strengths in mining (gold, platinum, diamonds) and financial services.
Johannesburg serves as the continent's leading financial hub.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Exceptional biodiversity, home to the 'Big Five' wildlife and Kruger National Park, one of Africa's largest game reserves.
The Cape Floristic Region is a UNESCO World Heritage biodiversity hotspot with extraordinary plant diversity.
Faces significant water-scarcity challenges in parts of the country.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Colonized by the Dutch and later the British from the 17th century onward.
The apartheid system of institutionalized racial segregation was formalized in 1948.
Apartheid was dismantled through negotiations in the early 1990s; Nelson Mandela became the first democratically elected president in 1994.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1994 marked the end of apartheid and the first democratic, all-race elections.
The 1996 Constitution is widely regarded as one of the world's most progressive, with an extensive Bill of Rights.
A parliamentary republic with three capital cities (Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein).

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: South African National Space Agency (SANSA) supports satellite and Earth-observation programmes.
A key partner in the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), one of the world's largest radio-telescope projects.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Rugby and cricket are hugely popular national sports.
Hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup, the first held on the African continent.
Rich musical traditions, including artists like Miriam Makeba, reflect the country's multicultural heritage.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of the African Union.
Member of the UN, G20, BRICS, and the Commonwealth of Nations; a leading voice for the African continent in global forums.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: South Africa is a parliamentary republic at Africa's southern tip, famous for ending apartheid in 1994 under Nelson Mandela, and the only African member of BRICS and G20.
keyFacts: Capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), Bloemfontein (judicial). Currency: South African Rand.
Parliamentary republic; President elected by the National Assembly.
Ended apartheid in 1994 with Nelson Mandela's ANC winning the first fully democratic elections.
Only African member of BRICS and G20.
commonConfusion: South Africa's President is elected by the National Assembly (parliament), NOT directly by popular vote — this distinguishes its system from many other presidential republics.

highYieldFacts: South Africa: parliamentary republic with three capital cities; ended apartheid in 1994.
Only African BRICS and G20 member.
India-South Africa: BRICS partners; deep historical link via Gandhi's 1893-1914 activism there; large Indian-origin community in Durban.
commonTraps: Assuming South Africa's President is directly elected by voters — the National Assembly elects the President.
Confusing South Africa's three-capital system as three separate seats of full government — each city handles a distinct branch (executive/legislative/judicial).
mustRemember: South Africa: post-apartheid 'Rainbow Nation', only African BRICS/G20 member, three capitals, deep Gandhi-era link with India.
